correctness.rationale: For all positive β,γ,N,φ and every point in the closed population simplex, s_+ and i_+ are nonnegative. The residual \(r_+\) is strictly decreasing in s at fixed i, hence minimal on the \(r=0\) face. There \(r_+=\frac{\tau i[1+\tau\rho-\tau\rho^2 i(1-i)]}{(1+\tau)(1+\tau\rho i)}\). Maximizing \(i(1-i)\) at \(i=1/2\) proves the iff bound \(\tau\rho(\rho-4)\le4\), including equality; solving the quadratic proves the exact unsafe interval. Exact witness \((\rho,\tau,s,i)=(5,1,1/2,1/2)\) yields \((1/7,7/8,-1/56)\). The standalone stdlib-only checker passed 15,981 exact-rational assertions; finite checks are supplemental, not universal proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source explicitly states the diagonal gain/loss map and warns that reconstructed R may fail nonnegativity, but does not derive the sharp quantitative global physical-rate criterion. Inspected older SIR schemes use different, often sequential conservative update rules, whose claims do not imply this same-map necessary-and-sufficient condition. Multiple literature and research-record queries sought aliases, parameter inequalities and the explicit negative witness; no covering theorem was identified. Historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent old-state gain/loss SIR positivity classification may exist in uncatalogued or inaccessible texts.
Uncertainty is greater for the 2021 original publisher version, where direct full publisher access was rate-limited; the available author-posted text was inspected.
The result is a sharp elementary specialization of a published algorithm, not a new general nonlinear positivity theorem.

value.rationale: The motivating source calls out the missing guarantee for the algebraically recovered population. This complete globally sharp invariant-simplex classification gives an actionable exact parameter/denominator threshold and unsafe initial-state geometry rather than an isolated counterexample or a generic orthant-positive statement. It directly separates a physical exact-rate scheme from independent fitted networks and prevents unsafe denominator selection when \(\beta N/\gamma>4\). The restriction to exact physical rates is central and explicitly stated; no downstream training-performance or broader control guarantee is claimed.
